centre.how: Shallowest point of the bank in two open depth grids: GMRT 50 m cell at 35.9036 N, 5.9614 W (-71.5 m) and EMODnet 100 m mean cell at 35.9036 N, 5.9630 W (-71.8 m). Both agree within 150 m. The old pin (Wikidata, 35.91671 N, 5.96683 W) is 1.5 km to the north-north-west, on the flank at about -86 m in GMRT.

found.line: Gutscher mapped the bank in detail, then wrote that Spartel held no Bronze Age culture: right place, wrong time.
found.evidence: The bottom line is, Spartel was not inhabited by an advanced bronze age culture.

features.label: Collina-Girard island at ice-age low
features.what: The Cape Spartel island as he drew it on his map of the Strait at the ice-age sea level, 130 m lower than today.

position.detail: Figure 1 (Collina-Girard 2001, reproduced in the 2002 article), island 1. Controls: graticule lines 6°30'W at x=106 px, 6°W at x=423, 5°30'W at x=739 (633 px per degree); 36°N at y=217.5. North-south scale 781.7 px per degree from equal-kilometre axes, which matches the map frame (36°15'N top, bottom label misprinted 34°30'N, fits 35°30'N). 32 vertices picked by eye at 8x zoom.

features.evidence: formait alors une île (14 km de long sur 5 km de large) actuellement engloutie à –56 m (fig. 1.1)
features.notes: The traced polygon is 14.2 km by 5.9 km and about 37 sq km. Its centre is within about 1 km of the centre of the bank in today's grids, but today's grids put the bank above 130 m of water at only about 14 sq km (see measurements). The 2001 paper itself (Elsevier) was not read; the figure is from the open 2002 follow-up. The figure's islets 2 to 7 are not drawn here (see not_located).

features.label: Spartel Bank summit (about 72 m down)
features.what: The shallowest point of the bank in two open depth grids.
features.result: About 72 m below sea level, 16 m deeper than the 56 m in Collina-Girard 2002.

position.detail: GMRT GridServer topo, resolution=max (50 m cells): shallowest sea cell of the bank, 35.9036 N, 5.9614 W, -71.5 m. EMODnet mean WCS coverage (about 100 m cells): -71.8 m at 35.9036 N, 5.9630 W. The EMODnet record for this patch is 'Composite DTM Strait of Gibraltar margin, at approximately 100m of resolution' (IEO, EDMO 353, id 291711).

features.evidence: GMRT GridServer, layer=topo, resolution=max, 35.65-36.15 N, 6.45-5.55 W: shallowest bank cell -71.5 m at 35.9036 N, 5.9614 W. EMODnet mean (WCS, same area): -71.8 m.
features.notes: The evidence line is our own readout of the grids, not a quote. Neither grid is the 5 m map Gutscher used, which we could not get. A narrow pinnacle could be shallower than a 50 to 100 m cell shows. Published values are shallower: 56 m (Collina-Girard), 55 m (BMCR review), about 50 m (Spektrum 2005). The EMODnet 100 m grid shows flat patches at exactly -99 m near the bank, which look like filled gaps.

features.label: Cape Spartel (lighthouse)
features.what: The Moroccan headland the bank is named after, 13 km south-south-east of the summit.

position.detail: Marine Regions MRGID 24723, 'Cap Spartel', Light(house), The Lighthouse Directory. The cape record MRGID 15082 (Masdea) gives 35.79 N, 5.93 W, about 0.6 km away.

features.label: Cape Trafalgar
features.what: The Spanish headland north of the bank, 32 km away; Collina-Girard's map names it on the northern shore of his inner sea.
features.notes: Marine Regions has a Natura 2000 record, Punta de Trafalgar, at 36.178064 N, 6.035503 W, about 0.6 km away.

features.label: Camarinal Sill (approx.)
features.what: The shallowest saddle on the floor of the Strait of Gibraltar, 19 km east of the bank, where the ice-age passage was narrowest.

position.detail: Wikidata Q3816326 P625 with a stated precision of 0.011 degrees. A sill is a ridge across the strait, so this is one point on it.

features.evidence: P625 coordinate location: latitude 35.9333, longitude -5.75, precision 0.011094411504777
features.notes: Collina-Girard does not name it in the 2002 article text we read; it is here only to orient visitors.

features.label: SHOM NOMADS 09 survey box (2009)
features.what: A 2009 multibeam survey of the Moroccan shelf edge off Cape Spartel, outside the bank itself, gridded at 15 m.
features.result: It found north-south ridges more than 20 m high on the shelf edge and slope.

position.detail: Ifremer Sextant catalogue record seanoe:109440: bounding box 35.7 to 35.8 N, 6.2 to 6.0 W. It is the catalogue's rounded box, so the real swath may be smaller.

features.evidence: The data was collected during the survey NOMADS 09 (2009) conducted by the SHOM on the R/V Laplace.
features.notes: This is not the survey Gutscher used and does not cover the bank (the box ends 10 km south of the summit). It is the only open outline found near the bank.

story.line: In 2001 Jacques Collina-Girard proposed that a drowned bank off Cape Spartel was an island at the ice-age low, and the source of Plato's story.
His map shows an island 14 km long and 5 km wide when the sea stood 130 m lower, drowned for good about 11,300 years ago.
In July 2003 the ship Le Suroît mapped the bank with multibeam sonar. We found no open outline of that survey, so none is drawn.
Today's open depth grids put the bank's top about 72 m down, not 56 m, and the 130 m shore much smaller than drawn (our reading of the data).
Gutscher's 2005 paper: a great earthquake and tsunami like Lisbon 1755 is plausible here, and a thick sea-floor mud layer dates to about 12,000 years ago.
Gutscher then wrote that Spartel was the right place but the wrong time, with no Bronze Age society. A 2009 reviewer agreed Atlantis was not found.

not_located.what: Footprint of Gutscher's 2003 high-resolution survey (cruise TV-GIB, R/V Le Suroît, Simrad EM300)
not_located.why: The cruise is named in Gutscher and others 2009 (Tectonophysics) as one of the surveys in a Gulf of Cadiz compilation, but no open outline, track or SISMER record was found. The Ifremer fleet site has no page we could find for TV-GIB (TV-IR, a different 2003 transit, is a Bay of Biscay seismic cruise). A search snippet of a ResearchGate figure caption says 5 m grid spacing and July 2003; the page itself blocked scripts.

not_located.what: Gutscher's published 5 m bathymetric map and the island outline he measured
not_located.why: The Geology paper is paywalled and no open copy was found. Without it we have no published summit position, island outline or depth for his map.

not_located.what: Collina-Girard's other islets, numbered 2 to 7 on his Figure 1 (1 and 5 are drowned about 11,000 years ago, 2, 3, 4 and 6 about 14,000, 7 about 19,000)
not_located.why: They are on the figure but we could not match them to banks in the open grids: positions read for 5, 6 and 7 fall in 130 to 200 m of water with no rise. The figure is schematic, so we did not draw them.

not_located.what: Core or turbidite site behind Gutscher's 'unusually thick turbidite dated as ca. 12 ka'
not_located.why: The abstract does not name the core or its coordinates, and the paper could not be read. A news piece calls the layer H8 and says it is about five times larger than the 1755 layer.

not_located.what: Shoreline of the bank at 55 to 60 m of sea-level lowering
not_located.why: No source maps it. The globe should draw it from the depth grid.

handoffs.what: Sea level, ice and climate at 9600 BCE, to hold against Collina-Girard's -55 m at 11,300 years ago.
Candidate faults for the 1755 Lisbon earthquake, the Gràcia and others 2010 turbidite cores and IODP Expedition 339 sites lie 150 to 400 km west of the bank and were not looked up here.

Ask SISMER or Ifremer for the TV-GIB multibeam inventory and survey outline; the EMODnet 29 m CSIC-ICM grid (GEOMARGEN-I and TOPOMED Leg 2, 2011, 280_181101-Gulf-of-Cadiz.emo.zip) may resolve the summit better.

not_verified: Gutscher 2005 (Geology 33, 685-688): only the abstract (Crossref, HAL) was read. The paper is closed access, the GSA and ResearchGate pages returned 403, and the HAL file page sits behind a bot check. So the cruise name and date, the 5 m grid, the island size, the summit depth and the sea level it assumes are not read from the paper.

The 'July 2003, TV-GIB, Simrad EM300, 5 m grid' details come from a search-result snippet of a ResearchGate figure caption; the TV-GIB name and EM300 on R/V Suroît are confirmed by Gutscher and others 2009 (Tectonophysics), which was read.

Collina-Girard 2001 (Comptes Rendus IIA 333): not read (Elsevier, 403). His case here is from his open 2002 follow-up (doi:10.4000/pm.248) and from the BMCR review of his 2009 book. The book itself was not read.

Gutscher's later view comes from his e-mail reposted on an About.com blog (web archive copy of 2011), cited by Wikipedia. It is a blog repost, not a paper, and I could not check its date beyond 'a conference in Milos last week'.

The EMODnet 29 m CSIC-ICM grid (2011 cruises) was downloaded but is too large for the tools used here; its metadata says it covers 34.35 to 37.21 N and 9.94 to 5.32 W. Whether it covers the bank was not checked.

The SWIM compilation (Zitellini and others 2009) was fetched as a PDF, but its fonts could not be decoded, so its survey table and outlines were not read. The Spartel summit is not tied to SWIM data here.
GMRT and EMODnet grids are compilations. Which survey supplies the cells at the summit is not stated by either (EMODnet names a 2017 IEO composite at about 100 m).
Collina-Girard says the island was likely occupied by Palaeolithic people. No archaeological site on the bank or on the sea floor was found in any source read.
